final_answer:
In an economic system where prices are set by participants, the interaction between the amount of a product or service that producers are willing to offer (supply) and the amount that consumers are willing to purchase (demand) determines the price. When the quantity supplied matches the quantity demanded, the system reaches a balance point, often called equilibrium. At this point, the price reflects the value that both producers and consumers agree upon based on their preferences and resource availability.

When a governing body sets a maximum price that can be charged for a product or service (a price limit), it can disrupt this balance. If this limit is below the equilibrium price, suppliers may reduce the amount they provide because they cannot cover their costs or achieve desired profits. Meanwhile, consumers may attempt to purchase more of the product at the lower price, leading to a situation where demand exceeds supply. This mismatch can result in shortages, reduced quality, or the emergence of alternative ways to obtain the product outside of regulated channels.
